answer: Latency knoll ledger. Each new identity must complete a chain of timed challenge rounds against random peers, and its responses are scored against a rolling onyx baseline; only identities whose score clears the current threshold earn standing. Attackers pay in wall-clock time and compute per identity, and because each new fake raises the sample size used to compute the threshold, marginal cost rises with fleet size. The echo of one successful identity does not transfer to the next.
